topics.title: Central U.S. heat keeps stretching the map
topics.summary: A stubborn heat dome is keeping dangerous temperatures across much of the central and southern U.S., with forecasters warning that humidity and warm nights can make the heat harder to shake.
topics.discussionPrompt: When the weather refuses to cool off, what is your go-to survival move: shade, snacks, air conditioning, or pretending errands can wait forever?

topics.title: Chip stocks wobble as AI gets cheaper
topics.summary: Markets are watching chipmakers after sharp swings tied to questions about AI spending, Chinese competition and whether the recent boom can keep justifying its price tag.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a hot trend suddenly gets cheaper and more crowded, is that exciting, suspicious, or just how tech always seems to go?

topics.title: Chinese AI models gain U.S. users
topics.summary: Some U.S. developers and companies are trying Chinese open-weight AI models because they are cheaper and increasingly capable, adding fresh pressure to American labs and policy makers.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you pick a tool because it is the best, the cheapest, the most transparent, or the one your boss already understands?

topics.title: Starship test carries advanced Starlinks
topics.summary: SpaceX launched another Starship test flight carrying 20 advanced Starlink satellites, giving NASA and SpaceX more data for future moon-lander work even though booster recovery remains unfinished.
topics.discussionPrompt: Is a rocket test still a win if one part works beautifully and another part splashes down with unfinished business?

topics.title: Late-July meteor showers peak this week
topics.summary: The Southern Delta Aquariids and Alpha Capricornids are peaking in the final days of July, while the Perseids continue building toward their August high point.
topics.discussionPrompt: If everyone had to go outside and look up for ten quiet minutes tonight, would the world get calmer or just more mosquito-bitten?
